title: Match a code
prompt: Implement `public static bool HasCode(string[] codes, string wanted)`. Return true only when one whole array item equals wanted using ordinal, case-insensitive comparison. Do not trim, use a substring match, or modify the array. Inputs are nonnull.
hints: Should a code with extra spaces count as the exact identifier?
Use `String.Equals` with `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase` on each whole array item.
Loop through the array and return true when `String.Equals(code, wanted, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` is true. Return false after the loop.
checkLabels: A complete code at a later array position must match even when its letter case differs.
A matching substring is not a complete code match.
Extra spaces must not be trimmed implicitly.
An empty array has no matching code.
A nonempty array with no matching code must return false.
Two empty identifiers are an exact match.
The method must not change the array.
Identifier matching must not depend on the current culture.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Accepts a wanted code contained inside a longer code.
Returns false after the first item instead of checking the rest.

feedback: Compare complete strings with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase. Do not trim or search inside the code.
